sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2018. Nominal affixes and number marking in the Plateau languages of Central Nigeria. In John R. Watters (ed.), East Benue-Congo: Nouns, pronouns, and verbs, 107-172. Berlin: Language Science Press. §2.8.2 Jilic, pp. 155-157.

sources.note: Nothing. The Jilic section gives Mijili singular/plural prefix pairings (Tables 66-68, adapted from Stofberg 1978: 316) with tone-marked forms; it notes 'There is a microfiched grammar of Mijili by Stofberg (1978)'. No word for stress/accent appears anywhere in the chapter.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2006. A Dictionary of the Jili (Migili) Language of Central Nigeria. Draft ms. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation, rogerblench.info.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: PHOIBLE's Jili inventory (PH 899, with tone contours) was extracted from this dictionary, so it contains a phonology sketch with a tone section; Blench's dictionary introductions typically also remark on stress/prominence. Open on rogerblench.info but the site is could not be reached by automated download and the exact path was not found (South Plateau page. exists).

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0 inventory PH 899 'Jili' (48 segments), source: Blench, Roger. 2006. A Dictionary of the Jili (Migili) Language of Central Nigeria. ms, rogerblench.info.
sources.note: Inventory page (phoible.org/inventories/view/899) lists tone contours ˦˥, ˥˩, ˩˥ and nasal vowels, i.e. a tone language per Blench's dictionary; nothing on stress. The underlying Blench 2006 dictionary itself could not be opened (rogerblench.info could not be reached by automated download).
